questions.skill: Derive arc length from similarity and define radian measure
questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: A central angle θ cuts off arc length s₁ on a circle of radius r₁ and arc length s₂ on a circle of radius r₂ (same center). Explain, using similarity, why s₁/r₁ = s₂/r₂.
questions.prompt_markup: A central angle θ cuts off arc length s₁ on a circle of radius r₁ and arc length s₂ on a circle of radius r₂ (same center). Explain, using similarity, why s₁/r₁ = s₂/r₂.
questions.required_method: Use the dilation about the center with factor r₂/r₁: it maps the first circle to the second and the first arc to the second arc.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof (paragraph, two-column, or flow). Essential: the dilation about the center with factor k = r₂/r₁ maps the first circle onto the second and the arc of angle θ onto the arc of angle θ; it multiplies all lengths, including arc length, by k; so s₂ = k s₁ and s/r is the same for both. This constant is θ in radians.

questions.prompt_markup: Use s = rθ to explain why a full turn is 2π radians and a half turn is π radians, and convert 270° to radians.
questions.correct_answer: A full turn cuts off the whole circumference 2πr, so θ = 2πr/r = 2π; half a turn cuts off πr, so θ = π; 270° is ¾ of a turn, 3π/2 radians.
